items.title: Detecting forever chemicals—with yeast and AI
items.excerpt: Researchers pair engineered yeast biosensors with AI analysis to detect PFAS 'forever chemicals' in samples.
items.rationale: New environmental-chemistry result that pairs engineered yeast biosensors with AI readout to detect PFAS. It is the freshest item in the pool and has no counterpart in the 30-day history.

items.title: X-Rays and AI Reveal How Spacecraft Heat Shields Burn in Real Time
items.excerpt: Berkeley Lab researchers combined X-ray imaging with AI analysis to watch spacecraft heat-shield material ablate in real time.
items.rationale: Berkeley Lab materials and space-engineering result in which AI analysis of X-ray imaging tracks heat-shield ablation as it happens. Adds a space and materials field.

items.title: Autonomous AI could create capacity for thousands more dermatology appointments, real-world study finds
items.excerpt: A real-world study of 8,391 patients found autonomous AI could free roughly 8,500 dermatology appointments over 16 months by safely discharging benign cases, with over 98% sensitivity for invasive melanoma.
items.rationale: Real-world clinical study of 8,391 patients with concrete outcome numbers (over 98% melanoma sensitivity, about 8,500 appointments freed). It was the strongest of the medical candidates.

items.title: AI chatbots give us a narrow slice of knowledge: Researchers warn of 'knowledge collapse'
items.excerpt: University of Copenhagen researchers found AI chatbots deliver significantly less diverse information than Google search across 155 topics, warning of 'knowledge collapse' as models train on AI text.
items.rationale: Empirical University of Copenhagen study across 155 topics that measures how much less diverse chatbot answers are than search results. A cognitive and information-science result, not opinion.

items.title: The tests that grade AI may be getting it wrong
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers analyzed 56 widely used AI benchmarks and found major measurement inconsistencies, including safety benchmarks that degrade across languages, arguing for measurement-science methods.
items.rationale: Stanford measurement-science audit of 56 AI benchmarks, with concrete findings such as safety benchmarks that degrade across languages. It is a different study from the 09-08 BenchMIRT post.
